newsitem.title: ROMANIA: TWO ROMANIAN BANKS CUT LEU INTEREST RATES.
newsitem.headline: TWO ROMANIAN BANKS CUT LEU INTEREST RATES.

text.p: Two large Romanian state- owned banks announced on Wednesday cuts in their interest rates on leu deposits and credits in line with an ease of the central bank's monetary policy following slowing inflation.
Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) will slash short-term lending rates to 53 from 62 percent starting July 24 in a bid to stimulate economic recovery, a bank statement said.
It said BCR rates on individuals' sight deposits would fall to an annual 15 from 18 percent, while three-month deposit rates would carry 53 percent annual interest, down from 65.
Another major bank, Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare (BRD), said it had lowered deposits rates this week, paying now 17 percent for individuals' sight deposits, down from 18 percent.
BRD -- the first Romanian state bank scheduled to turn private this year -- said it had cut three-month deposit rates to 59 percent from a previous 70 percent.
Rates on BCR one-year deposits fell to 62 from 76 percent, while the BRD pays now 70 percent interest on 12-month deposits, down from 76 percent previously.
Most interest rates on the Romanian market had slipped recently after monthly inflation eased to 2.3 percent last month from 4.3 in May and a record of 30.7 percent in March.
